title: Turn-of-the-Month: Window Dressing Behavior
one_line: Attributes part of the turn-of-the-month effect to institutional window dressing (buying winners / reducing risk into month-end reporting); related evidence (Rinne, Suominen & Vaittinen, 'Dash for Cash') puts the low point at T−8..T−4 and the gains at T−3..T+3 (S&P −3.4% vs +28.6% annualized).

findings.statement: Window dressing as a contributor to month-end / first-day returns.
Related: holding only the 7 turn-of-month days captured the full premium with ~half the volatility (1926-2013).

why.pattern: Institutional month-end cash needs and reporting incentives.

reported_results.headline: Attributes part of the turn-of-the-month effect to institutional window dressing (buying winners / reducing risk into month-end reporting); related evidence (Rinne, Suominen & Vaittinen, 'Dash for Cash') puts the low point at T−8..T−4 and the gains at T−3..T+3 (S&P −3.4% vs +28.6% annualized).

tradable_edge: Already covered by month_end_cash_cycle_es, month_end_rebalance_es and month_end_rebalance_pressure_es. No new spec.
data_fit: ES 1-min Dec 2013 → Sep 2026, NQ 1-min Jul 2021 → Sep 2026 (2024+ protected in the backtest project).
